title: Commute Time vs Baseline Anomaly
dataSources: ADS-B aircraft snapshots (`adsb:aircraft`), personal flight logbook (`flight:log`), commute trips (`commute:trip`), transit arrivals (`transit:arrival`), geofence events (`geofence:event`), travel documents (`travel:document`), fare quotes (`airprice:quote`).
app: Home ADS-B receiver (dump1090 / readsb / tar1090 JSON feed), personal flight logbook exports, commute/transit APIs, and phone geofence webhooks via Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=commute:trip
| eval dow=strftime(_time,"%A")
| eventstats avg(duration_min) as usual, stdev(duration_min) as sd by dow route
| eval worse_than_usual=if(duration_min>usual+2*sd,1,0)
| where worse_than_usual=1
| table _time route duration_min usual
description: Learns your normal commute time for each route and day of week, then flags the trips that were unusually slow.
value: A same-day-of-week baseline separates a genuinely bad traffic day from the ordinary Monday crawl, so alerts mean something.
implementation: Log each commute's duration and route to `index=personal`; schedule after your typical commute window and notify on anomalies.
visualization: Table of anomalous commutes with actual versus usual duration.
grandmaExplanation: It learns how long your commute normally takes and tells you when a trip was much slower than usual.
